title: State of AI Finance
dek_2026: How much money is flowing into and out of AI companies in 2026: venture funding and its concentration, frontier-lab valuations, revenue and losses, Nvidia's data-centre sales, the debt and equity financing the build-out, M&A and IPOs, and the indicators behind the bubble debate.

2024: Crunchbase counted more than $100 billion of venture funding to AI companies in 2024, about a third of the roughly $314 billion invested in startups worldwide that year.
OpenAI raised $6.6 billion at a $157 billion valuation in October 2024, and Databricks' $10 billion round in December 2024 was the largest venture raise of the year, according to Crunchbase.
Nvidia reported data-centre revenue of $115.2 billion for its fiscal year ended January 2025, roughly calendar 2024, up 142% on the year before.
OpenAI generated about $3.7 billion of revenue in 2024 and ended the year at an annualised run-rate of about $5.5 billion, according to figures the company confirmed in June 2025.
Anthropic's S-1, as reported by Reuters in 2026, shows revenue of roughly $400 million and an operating loss of $2.98 billion for 2024.
2025: Crunchbase counted $202.3 billion of venture funding to AI companies in 2025, close to half of the $425 billion invested globally; the OECD, using a broader definition, put AI's share at 61%, or $258.7 billion of $427.1 billion.

OpenAI's $40 billion round led by SoftBank in March 2025, at a $300 billion valuation, was the largest venture round of 2025, and an employee share sale in October 2025 valued the company at $500 billion.
OpenAI booked about $13.07 billion of revenue and a $20.92 billion operating loss in 2025, according to leaked audited accounts reported by the Financial Times.
Nvidia reported data-centre revenue of $193.7 billion for its fiscal year ended January 2026, roughly calendar 2025, up 68% on the year before.

Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle sold about $108 billion of bonds in 2025, according to a Reuters analysis of LSEG data, against an average of about $28 billion a year for the five hyperscalers in 2020–2024 (Bank of America).
2026: Crunchbase recorded $679 billion of global venture funding in the first nine months of 2026, a record for that period, with AI companies taking about 80% in the first quarter, more than 70% in the second and 64% in the third.

OpenAI closed a $122 billion round at an $852 billion post-money valuation on 31 March 2026, the largest private round on record, and on 6 November 2026 closed a first tranche of about $11 billion at a reported $1.25 trillion valuation.

Anthropic's public S-1, filed on 26 October 2026, reports revenue of $16.3 billion for the first half of 2026, up from about $1.2 billion a year earlier, and an operating profit of $974 million in the second quarter.
OpenAI told investors its annualised revenue was almost $50 billion at the end of September 2026, according to the Financial Times, CNBC and Reuters.

Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta reported about $207 billion of combined capital expenditure for July–September 2026, and between 26 October and 5 November 2026 Meta, Oracle and Alphabet raised more than $70 billion of new equity and debt, by Report AI's count.

2024: 2024 was the year AI became the venture market's centre of gravity. Crunchbase counted more than $100 billion of funding to AI companies, about a third of the roughly $314 billion invested worldwide, up more than 80% on 2023, and PitchBook put AI at 46.4% of US deal value. The money was concentrated. Databricks raised $10 billion, OpenAI $6.6 billion at a $157 billion valuation, and xAI $6 billion twice. A handful of labs and data platforms took the cheques that defined the year, while the rest of the venture market stayed close to its 2023 level.

Revenue was a small fraction of the spending it was meant to justify. OpenAI earned about $3.7 billion and reported losing roughly $5 billion, and Anthropic's S-1 shows about $400 million of revenue against a $2.98 billion operating loss. Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta spent about $246 billion on capital expenditure. By our crude gauge, that is about 60 dollars of big-tech capex for every dollar the two leading model makers earned. In June 2024 Sequoia's David Cahn called this gap 'AI's $600B question': the annual revenue the ecosystem would need to earn to pay for the build-out.

The clearest winner was the supplier. Nvidia's data-centre revenue reached $115.2 billion in the fiscal year to January 2025, up 142%, which made it the one company whose AI income was measurable rather than projected. Exits were scarce: no AI company of scale went public in 2024. Consolidation instead ran through acquisitions and licensing-and-hiring deals; Mergermarket counted $49.9 billion of M&A involving AI startups across 454 deals, both records. The financing pattern of the next two years was already set: private capital for the labs, operating cash flow for the hyperscalers, and very little public-market price discovery.
2025: In 2025 AI took roughly half of all venture money, and the exact share depends on who is counting. Crunchbase counted $202.3 billion, close to 50% of $425 billion; the OECD counted $258.7 billion, or 61% of $427.1 billion; PitchBook put AI at 65.4% of US deal value. These are differences of definition, not errors, and they should never be mixed in one series. What every tracker agrees on is concentration. OpenAI's $40 billion round at $300 billion was the largest of the year, and five companies each raised more than $5 billion, about a fifth of global venture funding.

Valuations moved faster than revenue. OpenAI went from $300 billion in March to $500 billion in an October employee share sale. Anthropic's last priced round was $183 billion in September, although the Microsoft and Nvidia investment in November implied about $350 billion. Revenue grew quickly but from a low base: OpenAI booked about $13.07 billion with a $20.92 billion operating loss, and Anthropic about $4.6 billion with an $8.06 billion operating loss. By year end their annualised run-rates were about $20 billion and $9 billion. The big four's capex reached about $410 billion, roughly 23 times the two labs' combined revenue.

The way AI was financed began to change. Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle sold about $108 billion of bonds, Meta's $27 billion Hyperion joint venture with Blue Owl became the largest private-credit deal on record, and Morgan Stanley put total data-centre debt issuance at about $182 billion. Nvidia agreed in September to invest up to $100 billion in OpenAI, which would buy Nvidia systems in return; the agreement was still unsigned in December. That deal made circular financing the year's main bubble argument. Public markets were cautious: CoreWeave's IPO raised $1.5 billion at $40 a share, below its target range.
2026: The scale of private funding in 2026 has no precedent. Crunchbase counted about $300 billion of global venture funding in the first quarter alone, and $679 billion over the first nine months, more than in any previous full year. By our calculation AI companies took about 72% of it, and PitchBook puts AI at 82.7% of US deal value. The largest single cheques went to frontier labs: OpenAI raised $122 billion at $852 billion in March, Anthropic $30 billion at $380 billion in February and $65 billion at $965 billion in May, and xAI $20 billion before it merged into SpaceX. Concentration, not breadth, explains the record.

Revenue is now arriving at scale, but the two leading labs do not report it on the same basis. Anthropic's S-1 shows $16.3 billion of revenue in the first half of 2026 and its first operating profit, $974 million, in the second quarter. OpenAI reported about $12.4 billion for the same half and a run-rate of almost $50 billion by September, compared with Anthropic's more than $65 billion at the end of July. Anthropic counts some cloud-partner revenue gross, and OpenAI does not, so a direct comparison is CONTESTED. Losses remain very large: OpenAI's operating loss was about $21.6 billion in the half year, and Anthropic's net loss of about $80 billion was mostly a non-cash charge.

The exit market reopened in 2026, and AI is driving it. Cerebras raised $5.55 billion in May. SpaceX, which absorbed xAI at a $250 billion valuation in February, raised $75 billion at $1.77 trillion in June. Days later it agreed to buy Cursor's maker, Anysphere, for $60 billion in stock, the largest acquisition of a venture-backed startup. Anthropic filed its public S-1 on 26 October without a price range. Outside the US, DeepSeek took outside money for the first time: about $7.4 billion around mid-year and about $15–16 billion in October, at a valuation reported between $74 billion and $90 billion.

The bubble indicators point in two directions. The ratio of big-four capex to the two labs' revenue has narrowed from about 60 times in 2024 to about 13 times on 2026 guidance, so the revenue gap is closing. How the spending is paid for, however, has become riskier. Hyperscaler bond issuance reached about $194 billion by early July, Meta raised about $35 billion of equity, Oracle paid coupons of up to 8.65%, and a data-centre loan backed by an Anthropic contract was marketed at 11% or more. Nikkei counts about $1.65 trillion of off-balance-sheet obligations. OpenAI's latest round priced at $1.25 trillion, below its $1.4–1.5 trillion ask.

takeaways_2026: Private capital hit records: $679 billion of global venture funding in January–September 2026 (Crunchbase), about 72% of it to AI by our calculation, led by OpenAI's $122 billion round at $852 billion.

Frontier-lab revenue is now measured in tens of billions: Anthropic reported $16.3 billion of revenue in H1 2026 in its 26 October S-1, and OpenAI's run-rate was almost $50 billion at the end of September; the two report on different bases.

Exits reopened: Cerebras ($5.55 billion, May), SpaceX including xAI ($75 billion at $1.77 trillion, June), SpaceX's $60 billion purchase of Cursor, and Anthropic's public S-1 make 2026 the first year of AI liquidity at scale.

The build-out is increasingly debt- and equity-financed: about $194 billion of hyperscaler bonds by July, more than $70 billion of new equity and debt from Meta, Oracle and Alphabet in late October–early November, and about $1.65 trillion of off-balance-sheet obligations (Nikkei).
yoy_takeaways: AI's share of global venture funding rose from about a third in 2024 to about half in 2025 and about 72% in January–September 2026 (Crunchbase basis; 2026 is Report AI's calculation from quarterly figures).

OpenAI's valuation rose from $157 billion (October 2024) to $500 billion (October 2025) to a reported $1.25 trillion (November 2026); Anthropic's priced valuation went from about $18 billion (early 2024) to $183 billion (September 2025) to $965 billion (May 2026).

Model-maker revenue grew far faster than capex: OpenAI's recognised revenue went from about $3.7 billion (2024) to $13.07 billion (2025), and Anthropic's from about $0.4 billion to $4.6 billion to $16.3 billion in H1 2026 alone, narrowing big-four capex per lab revenue dollar from about 60x to 23x to about 13x on 2026 guidance.

Nvidia's data-centre revenue went from $115.2 billion (fiscal year to January 2025) to $193.7 billion (to January 2026) to $164.2 billion in the first half of fiscal 2027 alone, while the financing of AI shifted from cash flow to bonds, equity and off-balance-sheet vehicles.

faq_2026.q: How much venture capital went into AI in 2026?
faq_2026.a: Crunchbase recorded $679 billion of global venture funding in January–September 2026, a record for any nine-month period. AI companies took about $242 billion (roughly 80%) in the first quarter, more than 70% of $205 billion in the second, and $102 billion (64%) in the third; Report AI calculates the year-to-date AI total at about $488 billion, or roughly 72%. PitchBook-NVCA puts AI at 82.7% of US deal value through September 2026.

faq_2026.q: What is OpenAI's valuation and revenue in 2026?
faq_2026.a: OpenAI closed a $122 billion round at an $852 billion post-money valuation on 31 March 2026, and on 6 November 2026 Bloomberg and Reuters reported a first close of about $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, below an earlier $1.4–1.5 trillion ask. OpenAI told investors its annualised revenue was almost $50 billion at the end of September 2026 (Financial Times, CNBC, Reuters); recognised revenue was about $12.4 billion in the first half of 2026, as reported by The Information.

Anthropic's public S-1, filed on 26 October 2026 for a Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT, reports revenue of $16.3 billion for the first half of 2026, up from about $1.2 billion a year earlier, $11.6 billion of revenue in the second quarter and a $974 million operating profit in that quarter. It also shows 2025 revenue of about $4.6 billion with an $8.06 billion operating loss. A half-year net loss of about $80 billion is mostly a non-cash fair-value charge. The filing sets no price range; Anthropic's last private valuation was $965 billion in May 2026.

faq_2026.q: Is AI a bubble? What do the financial indicators say?
faq_2026.a: The evidence cuts both ways. Revenue is catching up: Report AI calculates that Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta spent about 60 dollars of capex per dollar of OpenAI and Anthropic revenue in 2024, about 23 in 2025 and about 13 on 2026 guidance. Financing risk is rising: the four companies reported about $207 billion of capex in July–September 2026, free cash flow turned negative at Meta, Alphabet and Amazon, hyperscalers issued about $194 billion of bonds by early July 2026, and Nikkei counts about $1.65 trillion of off-balance-sheet obligations (July 2026). Circular deals, such as Nvidia's $30 billion stake in OpenAI's March 2026 round, mean that some demand is supplier-financed.

faq_2026.q: Which AI companies went public or were acquired in 2026?
faq_2026.a: Cerebras raised $5.55 billion at $185 a share in May 2026, the largest pure-play AI IPO of the year so far. SpaceX, which combined with xAI in February 2026 at a $250 billion valuation for xAI, raised $75 billion at a $1.77 trillion valuation when it listed on Nasdaq on 12 June 2026. SpaceX then agreed on 16 June 2026 to buy Anysphere, the maker of Cursor, for $60 billion in stock. Anthropic filed a public S-1 on 26 October 2026 but had not priced its offering as of 10 November 2026.
